events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.68 (model confidence 0.62)
events.body:
The trip is RydeTAXI and metered. One off-route segment is recorded: 08:42–08:54, 7.24 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.50 km, +4.74 km, peaking 1568 m off the optimal route [F3], against an overall +5.1 km / +37% over the estimate [F1][F2]. Under RD-1 the driver's duty is to take the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause, and the segment is reviewed against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [RD-1]. The RD-4 incident screen fails, so no traffic excuse arises [F15][RD-4].

RD-5 is the operative question, and the chat record is complete and timestamped (2 messages, both with times) [F10]. The driver proposed the change at 08:39 ("ok if I go round via Balestier Road?") [F8] and the rider answered at 08:40 "可以，走 Balestier Road 吧" — an express agreement to a SPECIFIC named road — both before the segment began at 08:42 [F9][RD-5]. Consent therefore exists and is the rider's own message; the driver's post-trip statement to the same effect [F11] is not needed, and a driver's claim would not have sufficed on its own [F11][RD-5].

The agreement is a named-road agreement ("走 Balestier Road"), so its scope is driving on Balestier Road only; a general route choice would have covered a route chosen to reach the destination, but this one is specific. On the record as it stands nothing ties the 08:42–08:54 segment to Balestier Road: the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, and the driver's statement [F11] also names Balestier Road and does not place the car elsewhere [F9][F11][RD-5]. Timing alone does not tie the segment to the named road, so under G13 the excess beyond what the agreed Balestier routing could reasonably cover is not settled by the record.

What the record does settle is the magnitude. Balestier Road runs roughly parallel to the CTE/upper Serangoon corridor and, as an alternative to that corridor, should sit within a few hundred metres of the optimal route; the fact table reports the segment reaching 1568 m (≈1.568 km) from the optimal route [F3]. Driving 1.568 km away from the optimal corridor is beyond what any Balestier Road routing can explain, so 1.568 km of the 4.74 km extra is not attributable to the agreed named road and is refundable under RD-2. The remaining ≈3.17 km (noise fit on the Balestier Road route) stands, treated against the driver [RD-2].

Amount: the distance rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km = $26.80 ÷ 19.01 km = $1.4098/km [F7][F4]; 1.568 km × $1.4098/km = $2.2106; plus the metre-unit excess billed beyond the segment's own extra_km, the excess-distance charge being $7.22 on 5.12 km at the same rate [F4], gives $7.22 × (1.568 ÷ 5.12) = $2.21; the waiting unit charged is $0.11 for 0.4 min on a metered taxi and is not refundable [F5][F7][RD-3]. The residual attributable distance, rounded to cents, is $6.68 [F4][RD-2].

No account flag arises: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days, and the driver's profile shows 0 upheld (route 0, no-show 0) [F18][RD-6].

The SAFE screen is negative: I read the complaint (a fare/route doubt, not an allegation of danger), both chat messages (a route proposal and a plain agreement) and the driver's statement (a claim of agreement) — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.68 to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the unexplained part of the Balestier Road detour; note that the driver's route-deviation duty under RD-1 was engaged (no account flag — no prior upheld dispute).

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver

RIDER: We reviewed your Balestier Road trip. You agreed in chat to a route via Balestier Road, but part of the detour went well beyond what that route can explain — about 1.6 km of the extra distance. We are refunding $6.68 for that portion, rounded to cents, paid as a Ryde voucher to your account. The rest of the extra distance stands as covered by your agreement, and the waiting charge stays. No action is needed from you.

DRIVER: We reviewed the Balestier Road trip. The rider did agree in chat to that specific road, so the trip is not treated as an unauthorised detour. However, part of the route went about 1.6 km beyond what a Balestier Road routing can explain, so $6.68 of the distance charge is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. Your account is not being flagged, since there is no prior upheld route dispute on it.

Consent therefore exists and is the rider's own message; the driver's post-trip statement to the same effect [F11] is not needed, and a driver's claim would not have sufficed on its own [F11][RD-5].

The agreement is a named-road agreement ("走 Balestier Road"), so its scope is driving on Balestier Road only; a general route choice would have covered a route chosen to reach the destination, but this one is specific. On the record as it stands nothing ties the 08:42–08:54 segment to Balestier Road: the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, and the driver's statement [F11] also names Balestier Road and does not place the car elsewhere [F9][F11][RD-5]. Timing alone does not tie the segment to the named road, so under G13 the excess beyond what the agreed Balestier routing could reasonably cover is not settled by the record.

What the record does settle is the magnitude. Balestier Road runs roughly parallel to the CTE/upper Serangoon corridor and, as an alternative to that corridor, should sit within a few hundred metres of the optimal route; the fact table reports the segment reaching 1568 m (≈1.568 km) from the optimal route [F3]. Driving 1.568 km away from the optimal corridor is beyond what any Balestier Road routing can explain, so 1.568 km of the 4.74 km extra is not attributable to the agreed named road and is refundable under RD-2. The remaining ≈3.17 km (noise fit on the Balestier Road route) stands, treated against the driver [RD-2].

Amount: the distance rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km = $26.80 ÷ 19.01 km = $1.4098/km [F7][F4]; 1.568 km × $1.4098/km = $2.2106; plus the metre-unit excess billed beyond the segment's own extra_km, the excess-distance charge being $7.22 on 5.12 km at the same rate [F4], gives $7.22 × (1.568 ÷ 5.12) = $2.21; the waiting unit charged is $0.11 for 0.4 min on a metered taxi and is not refundable [F5][F7][RD-3]. The residual attributable distance, rounded to cents, is $6.68 [F4][RD-2].

No account flag arises: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days, and the driver's profile shows 0 upheld (route 0, no-show 0) [F18][RD-6].

Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts.
